title.narrative: Security Assessment in North Africa (SANA) Project - Phase IV (Final Report)

description.narrative: The Security Assessment in North Africa (SANA) is a multi-year project of the Small Arms Survey. The project originated in 2012 in the aftermath of the Arab uprisings and the spread of armed conflicts and civil wars in North Africa. SANA aims to support actors engaged in building a more secure environment in North Africa and interlinked neighbouring regions. Over the course of its lifetime, the Project has and continues to produce timely, evidence-based research and analysis on the availability and circulation of small arms, the dynamics of armed groups, the trajectories of conflicts, and related insecurity. The research aims to enhance knowledge on small arms trafficking, armed violence, armed actors, and related measures and programmes. The Project’s main beneficiaries are policy-makers, practitioners, researchers, and journalists in both the region, and the international community. The current phase of the project—SANA IV —started in September 2021 and concluded in November 2024. This report is the final narrative report for SANA IV. Its purpose is to summarise and report on the activities and research funded by the Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Project No. 4000005126), covering the period 1 September 2021 to 15 November 2024. The project’s outcomes are examined in more depth in the external evaluation report for SANA IV, which is attached to this report.
